nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $0 < k \le n$, and let $d > 0$ be a real number. Then the number of pairs $(A, B)$ of finite sets of natural numbers such that $0 \in A$, the largest element of $A$ is $k$, the largest element of $B$ is $n - k$, and $|A + B| \le |A| + |B| + d$, where $A + B = \{a + b : a \in A, b \in B\}$ is the sumset, is at most $n^{2d+2} 2^k$.
nodes.title: Counting Boolean factor pairs with a small sumset

nodes.summary: Let $d : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be nondecreasing, and for a coefficient sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ write $d(f)$ for the sequence $k \mapsto d(f_k)$. Write $f \oplus g$ for the pointwise maximum and $f \otimes g$ for the max-min product of coefficient sequences $f$ and $g$. Then for all $f$ and $g$, $d(f) \oplus d(g) = d(f \oplus g)$ and $d(f) \otimes d(g) = d(f \otimes g)$.
nodes.title: Monotone digit maps are lunar homomorphisms

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $b$ be natural numbers and let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be a digit string with digits in $\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$. Then for every $k \ge n$, the $k$-th term of the coefficient sequence of $a$ is $0$.
nodes.title: A digit string has no coefficients beyond its length

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $b$ be natural numbers. The coefficient sequence of a digit string $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ with digits in $\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$ is the sequence $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ whose $k$-th term is $a_k$ for $k < n$ and $0$ for $k \ge n$.
nodes.title: Coefficient sequence of a digit string

nodes.summary: For every natural number $b \ge 2$, the lunar unit of base $b$, the sequence with constant term $b - 1$ and all other terms $0$, is a prime candidate in base $b$: its constant term is nonzero and one of its terms equals $b - 1$.
nodes.title: The lunar unit is a prime candidate

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a natural number. A coefficient sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is a prime candidate in base $b$ when its constant term $f_0$ is nonzero and some term $f_i$ equals $b - 1$, where the subtraction is truncated, so that $b - 1 = 0$ when $b = 0$. For $f$ with all terms less than $b$, the second condition says that the largest coefficient of $f$ is $b - 1$.
nodes.title: Lunar prime candidates

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $b \ge 2$ be natural numbers, let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be a digit string with digits in $\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$, and let $f$ be its coefficient sequence. If $f$ is a prime candidate in base $b$ and $f$ is max-min indecomposable, then $f$ is a lunar prime of base $b$.
nodes.title: Indecomposable prime candidates are lunar primes

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a natural number. The lunar unit of base $b$ is the constant polynomial $b - 1$, the sequence with constant term $b - 1$ and all other terms $0$. A coefficient sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is a lunar prime of base $b$ (Applegate, LeBrun and Sloane) when for all sequences $g, h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with all terms less than $b$ and $g \otimes h = f$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min…
nodes.title: Lunar primes

nodes.summary: A coefficient sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is indecomposable (in the arXiv version: irreducible) when for all sequences $g, h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $g \otimes h = f$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min product, $g$ or $h$ is a max-min monomial, that is, a sequence with exactly one nonzero term.
nodes.title: Max-min indecomposable sequences

nodes.summary: For every natural number $b \ge 2$, the lunar unit of base $b$, the sequence with constant term $b - 1$ and all other terms $0$, is a max-min monomial: it has exactly one nonzero term.
nodes.title: The lunar unit is a monomial

nodes.summary: A coefficient sequence $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ over the max-min semiring is a monomial when exactly one of its entries is nonzero, that is, when it is $c x^i$ for some index $i$ and some coefficient $c \neq 0$.
nodes.title: Monomials over the max-min semiring

nodes.summary: Fix an integer $b \ge 2$. There is a constant $C > 0$ such that for every integer $n \ge 2$ and all reals $d > 0$ and $v > 0$, the set $\Sigma_b^n$ of decomposable lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$ satisfies
nodes.title: Upper bound on the number of decomposable lunar numbers

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $b$ and $n$, let $\mathcal{L}_b^n$ be the set of lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$, that is, polynomials $c_0 \oplus c_1 x \oplus \dots \oplus c_n x^n$ with digits $c_k \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$. The set $\Sigma_b^n$ of decomposable lunar numbers consists of the $h \in \mathcal{L}_b^n$ that factor as $h = f \otimes g$ under the max-min product, with $f, g \in \mathcal{L}_b^n$ each…
nodes.title: Decomposable lunar numbers

nodes.summary: Fix an integer $b \ge 2$. There is a constant $C > 0$ such that for every integer $n \ge 1$ and every real $d > 0$, the set $\mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ of $d$-Hoeffding extremal lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$ has at most $C n^2 e^{-d^2/(4(n+2))} b^n$ elements.
nodes.title: Bound on the number of Hoeffding extremal lunar numbers

nodes.summary: Let $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers and $d$ a real number. Let $\mathcal{L}_b^n$ be the set of lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$ (digit strings $c_0, \dots, c_n$ with digits in $\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$), with the max-min product $\otimes$, and for $f \in \mathcal{L}_b^n$ let $|f_i|$ be the number of its digits that are at least $i$. The set $\mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ of $d$-Hoeffding extremal lunar numbers…
nodes.title: Hoeffding extremal lunar numbers

nodes.summary: Fix an integer $b \ge 2$. For a natural number $n$ let $\mathcal{I}_b^n = \Sigma_b^n \setminus \mathcal{D}_b^n$, where $\Sigma_b^n$ is the set of decomposable lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$ and $\mathcal{D}_b^n$ the set of level-decomposable ones, and for a real $d$ let $\mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ be the set of $d$-Hoeffding extremal ones. There is a constant $C > 0$ such that for every natural number…
nodes.title: Bound on decomposable lunar numbers neither level decomposable nor extremal

nodes.summary: For the base-$3$ lunar number $f = 1 \oplus 2x^2$ of degree at most $2$, with digits $1, 0, 2$, exactly two digits are at least $1$ and exactly one digit is at least $2$: $|f_1| = 2$ and $|f_2| = 1$.
nodes.title: Level counts of $1 \oplus 2x^2$ in base $3$

nodes.summary: Let $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers, $d$ a real number and $f, g, h$ lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$ with $h = f \otimes g$ under the max-min product. For a natural number $i$ write $|f_i|$, $|g_i|$ and $|h_i|$ for the numbers of digits of $f$, $g$ and $h$ that are at least $i$. If $h$ is not in the set $\mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ of $d$-Hoeffding extremal lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$,…
nodes.title: Level counts of a product that is not Hoeffding extremal

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a lunar number of base $b$ and degree at most $n$, with digits $c_0, \dots, c_n \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$, and let $i$ be a natural number. The level count $|f_i|$ is the number of indices $k \le n$ with $c_k \ge i$, that is, the number of nonzero coefficients of the $i$-level support $f_i = s_i(f)$, the Boolean polynomial with coefficient $1$ at $x^k$ when $c_k \ge i$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Level counts of a lunar number

nodes.summary: Let $b \ge 2$ and $n$ be natural numbers and $d > 0$ a real number. The number of elements of $\mathcal{D}_b^n \setminus \mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ is at most $n^{2d+4} 2^{d/2-n/3} b^{n+1}$, where $\mathcal{D}_b^n$ is the set of level-decomposable lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$ and $\mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ is the set of $d$-Hoeffding extremal ones.
nodes.title: Bound on level-decomposable lunar numbers that are not Hoeffding extremal

nodes.summary: Let $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers and $a = \lfloor b/2 \rfloor$. For a lunar number $f$ of base $b$ and degree at most $n$, given by its digits $f_0, \dots, f_n \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$, write $|f_a|$ for the number of indices $k \le n$ with $f_k \ge a$. The set $\mathcal{D}_b^n$ consists of the lunar numbers $h$ of base $b$ and degree at most $n$ such that $h = f \otimes g$ for some lunar numbers $f$ and $g$ of…
nodes.title: Level-decomposable lunar numbers

nodes.summary: Let $b \ge 2$ and $n$ be natural numbers and let $d > 0$ and $v > 0$ be reals. Count the lunar numbers $h$ of base $b$ and degree at most $n$ that lie in $\Sigma_b^n \setminus \mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ (decomposable but not $d$-Hoeffding extremal) and can be written as $h = f \otimes g$, with $\otimes$ the max-min product, where $f$ and $g$ are lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$, each with at least two…
nodes.title: Decomposable lunar numbers with a low-degree factor

nodes.summary: Fix an integer $b \ge 2$. For $n \ge 1$ let $\pi_b(n)$ be the number of digit strings $(a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ with $a_k \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$ and leading digit $a_{n-1} \ne 0$ whose coefficient sequence $(a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}, 0, 0, \dots)$ is a lunar prime of base $b$; these are the prime lunar numbers of base $b$ with $n$ digits. Then $\pi_b(n) \sim (b - 1)^2 b^{n-2}$ as $n \to \infty$, as conjectured by…
nodes.title: Asymptotic count of lunar primes

nodes.summary: For a natural number $b$, the lunar unit of base $b$ is the coefficient sequence $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ whose constant term is $b - 1$ and whose other terms are all $0$, that is, the constant polynomial $b - 1$ over the max-min semiring. The subtraction is truncated, so the lunar unit of base $0$ is the zero sequence.
nodes.title: Lunar unit

nodes.summary: Fix an integer $b \ge 2$. For each $n$, among the polynomials of degree $n$ with coefficients in $\mathcal{B}_b = \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$, that is, coefficient strings $(a_0, \dots, a_n)$ with $a_n \ne 0$, the proportion of those that are indecomposable over the max-min semiring tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Almost all max-min polynomials are indecomposable

nodes.summary: For all sequences $g, h \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the max-min product satisfies $(g \otimes h)_1 = \max(\min(g_0, h_1), \min(g_1, h_0))$.
nodes.title: Linear coefficient of a max-min product

nodes.summary: For all sequences $g, h \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the max-min product satisfies $(g \otimes h)_0 = \min(g_0, h_0)$.
nodes.title: Constant coefficient of a max-min product

nodes.summary: The max-min product of sequences $g, h \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is the sequence $g \otimes h$ with $(g \otimes h)_k = \max_{i + j = k} \min(g_i, h_j)$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the maximum running over pairs of natural numbers $(i, j)$. This is the product of the max-min semiring $(\mathbb{N}, \max, \min)$ on coefficient sequences.
nodes.title: Max-min product

nodes.summary: In base $2$, the lunar number with digit string $(1, 1, 1)$, that is $1 \oplus x \oplus x^2$ with $\oplus$ the lunar sum (digitwise maximum), lies both in the set $\Sigma_2^2$ of decomposable lunar numbers of degree at most $2$ and in the set $\mathcal{D}_2^2$ of level-decomposable lunar numbers of degree at most $2$.
nodes.title: A decomposable lunar number in base 2

nodes.summary: For every integer $b \ge 2$, the zero sequence is not a lunar prime of base $b$: $0 = 0 \otimes 0$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min product, and $0$ is not the lunar unit, the constant polynomial $b - 1$ with coefficient sequence $(b - 1, 0, 0, \dots)$.
nodes.title: Zero is not a lunar prime

nodes.summary: The zero coefficient sequence $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is not indecomposable over the max-min semiring: it factors as $0 = 0 \otimes 0$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min product, and the zero sequence is not a monomial.
nodes.title: The zero sequence is decomposable

nodes.summary: The zero coefficient sequence $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is not a max-min monomial: a monomial has exactly one nonzero entry, and the zero sequence has none.
nodes.title: The zero sequence is not a monomial

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, consider the Boolean polynomials of degree exactly $n$ with nonzero constant term, that is, the base-$2$ lunar numbers given by digit strings $(a_0, \dots, a_n) \in \{0, 1\}^{n+1}$ with $a_0 \ne 0$ and $a_n \ne 0$. The proportion of these which are lunar primes in base $2$ tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Shitov's theorem: almost all Boolean polynomials with nonzero constant term are prime

nodes.summary: In base $2$, the zero lunar number of degree at most $2$ (the digit string $(0, 0, 0)$) lies in the $1$-Hoeffding extremal set $\mathcal{H}_2^2(1)$: for the level $i = 1$, the number $|0_1|$ of its digits that are at least $1$ is $0$, and $\left|0 - (2 - 1) \cdot 2 / 2\right| = 1 > 1/2$.
nodes.title: An example of a Hoeffding extremal lunar number
